newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek troops begin leaving for chaotic Albania.
newsitem.headline: Greek troops begin leaving for chaotic Albania.

text.p: The first Greek troops in a multi-national force to safeguard humanitarian aid in chaotic Albania left on Wednesday for Tirana and the western port of Vlore.

About 110 soldiers were flown on C-130 planes from the northern Greek city of Salonika to Tirana and the Greek navy tank-landing ship Samos sailed with another 130 troops, defence ministry sources said.
The Samos, which is also carrying tanks, transport vehicles and other equipment, is expected to reach Vlore on Friday.
Greece, concerned with the crisis on its northern border, has pledged about 700 men to the Italian-led eight-nation force of 6,000 soldiers.
The rest of the Greek troops will leave for Albania in the next few days, the sources said.
The U.N.-approved force, codenamed "Operation Alba" - the Italian word for "dawn" - began arriving by air and sea on Tuesday.
Its mission is to prepare the way for the arrival of much-need aid to the impoverished Balkan country, which has been racked by violence since the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes.
Some 300 people have been killed and 700 injured during the weeks of armed anarchy and banditry that have swept Europe's poorest nation.
